stories.author: thepoet
stories.title: Kobo can run apps now
stories.groq_label: Kobo e-readers now support third-party apps via Cobalt, an open-source platform with a Rust SDK, running static ARM binaries in isolated processes and installing updates over Wi-Fi.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – Community Perspective:

The Hacker News community generally responded to this project enabling apps on Kobo e-readers with positive reactions. Many commenters appreciated the increased functionality and customization options, considering it useful because it allows users to run apps like Firefox, Syncthing, and KOReader, and even author their own applications. Others highlighted the potential for integrating services like Libby or Zotero, or improving highlight management and search capabilities. Nevertheless, recurring criticisms focused on the potential for distraction and the departure from the simplicity of traditional e-readers, with some questioning whether this aligns with the core purpose of an e-reader as a distraction-free reading device. As a whole, commenters viewed the project as an interesting contribution while acknowledging that it still has room for improvement, particularly in balancing functionality with the minimalist reading experience.
stories.groq_explain: Kobo e-readers can now run third-party apps thanks to Cobalt, an open-source platform that turns the device into a mini computer. It’s like installing an app store on your e-reader—apps install, update, and remove wirelessly, and you can always go back to the normal Kobo reader. The apps are secure, running in isolated processes, and don’t mess with the device’s core functions. It matters because it turns a simple e-reader into a more versatile tool for reading, coding, or browsing without needing extra hardware.
